correctness.rationale: The theorem quantifies over every finite nonempty reflexive monotone factor pair and every valuation. Forward mix is direct upward closure. Reverse mix sufficiency uses a singleton or a finite nonempty meet of qualifying sections; necessity uses a minimal horizontal neighborhood and incompatible vertical section pair. Two explicit pointed products realize sharp six- and nine-world bounds, with lower bounds proved by two-point intersection-closure. The code independently enumerates all pointed local families and all valuations through 3-by-3 (including 12800 3-by-3 configurations), but finite testing is not used in lieu of the general proof.

originality.rationale: Primary 2026 three-modal product semantics is formulated for normal neighborhood filters. Its forward mix and the known finite-normal collapse do not cover the finite nonnormal characterization or sharp failure products. Full-text comparisons with a normal rectangularization theorem and older two-modal monotone and normal product literature found no implication of the new claim. Priority uncertainty remains for unindexed alternative terminology.
residual_risks: A historically unindexed treatment of nonnormal monotone three-modal rectangle products might establish the same small threshold under different terminology.

value.rationale: A natural and complete local criterion tells precisely when the mixed coordinate-quantification modality can be replaced by the rectangle modality on every finite monotone reflexive full product. It identifies how weakening normality to monotonicity changes the finite structural behavior and proves exact minimum product cardinalities for individual and simultaneous failures; these are natural logical resource thresholds, not arbitrary parameter choices.
